profiles.Summary: Halo Infinite runs on the Steam Deck via Proton but requires significant settings reductions to achieve playable frame rates, as the Deck's GPU sits right at the PC minimum spec tier. The open-world campaign is the most demanding portion; multiplayer modes tend to run somewhat better due to smaller, more controlled environments.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (RX 570 / GTX 1050 Ti class, which closely matches the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU) and general Deck hardware capabilities. On first launch, check the frame counter in the first open-world area and in a multiplayer match — if you see sustained dips below 30 fps, drop to the Max Battery profile and reduce render resolution further.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 800p keeps GPU load manageable; the 8 W TDP limit and locked 900 MHz GPU clock reduce heat and power draw. Expect shader stutter on first launch until the cache is built.

The game uses DirectX 12 exclusively, which can cause shader compilation stutters on first run — expect stutter until shaders are cached.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Multiplayer arenas are more likely to sustain 55-60 fps at these settings; the open-world campaign will dip to 40-50 fps in large outdoor areas. Do not raise settings above Medium — the Deck's GPU cannot sustain High or Ultra at any playable frame rate.

Optimal.Notes: A modest resolution bump to 1024x640 with FSR upscaling gives a noticeably cleaner image while keeping frame pacing stable at 30 fps. Texture Quality at Medium is the best single setting to raise for visual quality at low cost.

Occasional crashes or black screens reported; switching to GE-Proton or Proton Experimental typically improves stability.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At full TDP with a 40 Hz refresh rate lock, the Deck can push a more detailed image with some Medium settings, though busy outdoor areas and large firefights may dip toward 35 fps. Drop Geometry and Shadow Quality back to Low if frame pacing becomes inconsistent.
